seoTitle: How to Delete or Hide a Conversation on Slack
metaDescription: Delete individual Slack messages, mute or hide a direct message, or archive a channel — and see who can and can't see it disappear.
intro: Slack doesn't give you a single button that wipes a conversation off the face of the earth for both sides. For direct messages, that's by design: the other person's copy of the history is theirs to keep. What you do control is your own message content and your own sidebar view. You can permanently delete anything you personally posted, mute or hide a noisy conversation, and archive a channel to freeze it in place. This guide separates those three different actions so you pick the right one instead of assuming a muted DM is the same as a deleted one.
costNote: Deleting a message, muting a DM, and archiving a channel are free on every Slack plan. Custom message-retention timelines are not: the Free plan only offers a 90-day or one-year choice, a specific day count needs Pro or above, and org-wide enforcement needs Enterprise Grid.

steps.heading: Understand what 'delete' removes
steps.body: Deleting only ever applies to content personally posted: a message, a file, a formatted block, unless the person doing it is a workspace admin with permission to remove other members' content. For a regular member it's permanent. Once confirmed, there's no built-in undo, and the message disappears from the conversation for everyone who can see that channel or DM, not just from your own view. This is the tool for fixing a mistake or pulling something sensitive, not for clearing an entire conversation's history.

steps.heading: Delete an individual message
steps.body: Hover over the message to remove until the hidden action icons appear along its right edge, then click the three-dot 'More actions' menu and choose Delete message. Slack shows a confirmation warning before it commits, since this step can't be walked back afterward. Do this one message at a time. There's no native bulk-delete across a whole conversation in the standard interface, so clearing a long thread this way is a message-by-message process.

steps.heading: Mute or hide a direct message, not delete it
steps.body: If the goal is decluttering your own view rather than erasing anything, Slack's documented way to do that is muting, not a simple close icon on the sidebar entry. Open the DM, click its notification icon, and mute it; for a group DM you'll see a specific Mute and hide option. Muting a one-person DM hides it automatically once your sidebar preferences are set to hide muted conversations. None of this deletes a single message on either side. It only changes what shows in your own sidebar, and the setting follows your account across devices, not just one browser. If the goal is to stop seeing a specific person's messages everywhere, not just in one DM, Slack has a separate 'Hide a person' option from their profile menu. That's a broader action: it hides their messages across shared channels too, not only the direct conversation, so it's a blunter tool than most people reach for when they just want a tidier sidebar.

steps.heading: Archive a channel instead of a DM
steps.body: Channels work differently from direct messages, since they're shared team spaces, not two-person threads. Open the channel, click its name in the header, open Settings, and choose Archive channel for everyone, then confirm. By default, any member who isn't a guest can archive a channel they belong to, and a channel's assigned managers can always archive it regardless of that setting; workspace owners can restrict the permission to specific roles. Archiving freezes the channel: no new messages can be posted, but its full history stays searchable and viewable instead of being deleted outright, which makes it the safer choice when a project wraps up.

steps.heading: Set a workspace-wide retention policy
steps.body: For ongoing cleanup instead of one-off deletions, workspace admins can set message retention under Slack's data retention settings, but how much control depends on the plan. On the Free plan, an owner can only choose between keeping data 90 days or one year; there's no arbitrary custom day count. Pro and Business+ support genuinely custom retention timelines set by workspace owners, with Business+ able to delete messages from channel view while keeping them in exports. On Enterprise Grid, org owners can set retention org-wide, and workspace owners can adjust it locally where allowed. This is the tool for keeping storage and search results lightweight over time without anyone manually deleting anything themselves, and unlike message-by-message deletion, it applies uniformly instead of depending on individual members remembering to clean up.

troubleshooting.cause: Muting a one-person DM only hides it automatically if sidebar preferences are set to hide muted conversations, and any new message from that person un-hides it.
troubleshooting.fix: Check Preferences for the option to hide muted conversations, and expect the thread to resurface the moment the other person messages again.

troubleshooting.problem: An admin can't delete a message in someone else's direct message.
troubleshooting.cause: Admins can delete other members' messages in public channels, private channels, and group DMs they're part of, but not in a one-person DM between two other members, since the admin was never part of that conversation.
troubleshooting.fix: There's no admin override for a private 1:1 DM. The only way that message goes away is if the person who sent it deletes it.

troubleshooting.problem: A 30-day retention rule can't be set.
troubleshooting.cause: Custom day-count retention is a Pro-and-above feature. The Free plan only offers a binary choice between 90 days and one year.
troubleshooting.fix: Upgrade the plan, or use one of the two Free-plan retention options instead of a custom count.

faq.question: Can I delete a message someone else sent?
faq.answer: Only workspace admins can delete other members' messages, and only in channels, private channels, or group DMs they're part of. A one-person DM between two other members is outside admin reach.

faq.question: Does hiding a DM delete the conversation history?
faq.answer: No. Muting a DM (or hiding it, for a group DM) only changes your own sidebar view. The full history reappears the moment that contact messages you again.

faq.question: Is there a time limit for deleting a message?
faq.answer: Slack generally lets you delete your own messages at any time, though some workspaces set policies that restrict this.

faq.question: Can I recover a deleted message?
faq.answer: No. Deleting a message is permanent for regular members; there's no built-in undo once it's confirmed.

faq.question: What's the difference between archiving a channel and deleting a message?
faq.answer: Archiving freezes a channel so nothing new can be posted, but its full history stays intact and searchable. Deleting a message removes that specific content for good.

faq.question: Can I set a custom retention period like 30 days?
faq.answer: Only on Pro and above. The Free plan only offers a choice between keeping data 90 days or one year, not an arbitrary day count.
